name: Sound of the Goddess - Chanting | Listening | Reflection
description:
Join Nina Rao (international chantress & seeker) and Neha Bhat (award winning author & sex therapist) for an intimate afternoon of chant, storytelling, and deep reflection on the Sacred Feminine. We'll be singing, reflecting and listening in-depth together!
About the Event
Join international chant leader Nina Rao and psychotherapist Neha Bhat for an intimate afternoon where ancient devotional traditions meet contemporary emotional understanding. Together, we will explore the many faces of the Divine Feminine through chant, reflection, and depth psychology.
Rather than looking at the stories of Devi as distant mythology, we will discover how they serve as living psychological wisdom, illuminating our modern experiences with grief, courage, boundaries, sexuality, healing, and belonging.
What to Expect
The afternoon will seamlessly weave together:
- Guided devotional chanting and mantra practice
- Reflective dialogue and storytelling
- Interactive audience conversation
- Contemplative practices and somatic insights
No prior experience with chanting or meditation is necessary. All are welcome.
About the Facilitators
Nina Rao brings the experiential, devotional, and embodied practice of mantra and Bhakti. Rooted in traditional chanting and years of teaching alongside Krishna Das, she speaks beautifully on the Sacred Feminine, nature, and contemplative practice.
Neha Bhat, ABT, ATR-P brings the lenses of contemporary psychology, sexual wellness, archetypal thinking, and the emotional landscapes of modern womanhood
Date: Thursday, November 5, 2026
Time: 3:00 PM – 5:30 PM
Ticket: ₹650 per person | You'll recieve a confirmation within two business days.
Simple refreshments will be provided.
For event related enquiries please email: assistant@chantkirtan.com

name: Sacred Music for Sacred Forests Concert - Save Wild Tigers and Their Habitats | Satsang | Kirtan
description:
Join us for an evening of kirtan, music, and satsang with Nina Rao and Friends to raise awareness and funds for saving wild tigers and their habitats across India - the Land of the Tiger.
India is the last viable habitat for wild tigers and one of the most biologically diverse regions in Eurasia.
Protecting this ecosystem means safeguarding not just tigers, but also elephants, langurs, deer, birds, rivers, plants, and the sacred balance of nature itself.
This concert is a celebration of India’s living tradition of honoring wildlife as sacred embodiments of Mother Earth. Through intentional prayer, chanting, and community, let us come together to protect nature and give thanks. We will also share a few words about some of the critical work being done to protect India’s wildlife and wild lands.
Schedule
- 6:30 PM – Doors open for general admission seating (Please bring your own pillow if you wish to sit on the floor; chairs are also provided at the venue)
- 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM – Sacred Music for Sacred Forests Concert with Nina Rao & Friends
About Nina Rao & Saving Wild Tigers
Nina Rao (via SavingWildTigers.org) has been supporting tiger conservation in India since 1998, guided by renowned conservationists including the late Valmik Thapar, Dr. K. Ullas Karanth, Dr. Krithi K. Karanth, and Dr. Dharmendra Khandal.
Where Your Funds Go
All funds raised from this concert will go directly to community-based conservation projects focused on human-wildlife co-existence. Proceeds will be distributed evenly to support the following charity partners:
- Centre for Wildlife Studies, Bengaluru (CWS India) & Tiger Watch: Funding critical, grassroots conservation efforts to protect tigers and foster safe coexistence between wildlife and local communities.
- Go Dharmic (The Dharma Forest): Supporting the massive rewilding initiative in the Sundarbans to plant mangroves, which restore natural habitats and shield coastal communities.
Community Support: We believe this sacred music should be accessible to all. If you wish to join but require financial assistance, please email us at sandip@godharmic.com to request a community discount code.

name: Flying Tigers - Vikalp Bengaluru Presents
description:
Flying Tigers
A film by Madhusree Dutta
105 minutes | 2026 | Bengali, English, Mandarin, German with English subtitles
About the Film:
The term Flying Tigers originates from a massive US military logistical operation connecting India and China across Himalayas during World War II. This story resurfaced after 70 years, when mother of the director was diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and kept saying  - Close the Windows / Tiger is Coming. The film traces various renditions of flying tiger by permeating through memories of territories, wars, and infrastructure projects. Following the il-logic of Alzheimer’s disease the film insistently shifts between lenses and perspectives, and slides across locations.
About the Filmmaker:
Madhusree Dutta is a filmmaker, author and cultural producer living in India and Germany.
Her area of interest are hybridity within public and urban culture as well as documentary and archival practices. She is the founder and former director (1998 - 2016) of Majlis, a center for interdisciplinary art initiatives in Mumbai; and former artistic director (2018 - 2021) of Academy of the Arts of the World (Akademie der Künste der Welt), in Cologne, Germany.
With Flying Tigers Madhusree Dutta returns to filmmaking after twenty years.
The screening will be followed by a QnA session with Director, Madhusree Dutta.
About Vikalp Bengaluru:
Vikalp Bengaluru is a collective of documentary filmmakers screening the best in non-fiction films in Bengaluru for over two decades. Read more here - https://vikalpbengaluru.weebly.com/

name: Block Party! - A special event curated by Sabha Blr for Children's Day - Nov 13
description:
Come spend a day at Sabha where childhood takes centre stage.
Our Block Party is a celebration of play, imagination, stories, making and, most importantly, simply being a child. Bring the whole family for a day packed with things to discover, create and get a little messy with.
Explore construction play with Troy Blocks. Expect storytelling sessions and book readings by child authors, hands-on building and tinkering with Tinkernauts, sensory play by Luna Sole, and a food market filled with healthy, delicious options for little ones. There will also be arts and crafts, face painting, tattoos and plenty more to keep curious minds and busy hands occupied.
Panel discussions by children, for children. Music and performances by little prodigies and so much more!
Whether your child loves making things, listening to stories, getting creative, exploring with their senses or simply running around and meeting new people, there will be something for them.
At Sabha, we believe that spaces for children should be spaces for all children. The Block Party is designed to welcome children of different backgrounds, interests and abilities, and to create a day where everyone can participate, explore and feel at home.
Open to all ages | Curated for 0 - 10
Construction Play | Flea Market | Story Telling | Book Readings | DIY Arts and Crafts | Face Painting | Music | Sensory Play | Food

name: Theatre Festival: Opening & Two Shows
description:
About the Festival
PLAYINTERPLAY is a theatre festival with a difference. It celebrates 50 years of the Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation, bringing together its theatre awardees and scholars to show their work, share their experiences, skills and learnings, and converse on matters of common interest.
PLAYINTERPLAY presents plays that are new to Bengaluru. What is different, however, is that it looks back as well as forward, featuring a work of theatre that has been specially revived for the festival and readings of plays that are still to become the finished article.
PLAYINTERPLAY does more: it forges connections between its constituent parts — performances, workshops, conversations and experience sharing — emphasising the interplay between thought, learning and practice.
See the plays! Apply for the workshops! Join the conversations! Soak in the magic of theatre.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROGRAMME
Please be in your seats by 4:15 p.m.
Opening Address - 4.30 p.m. – 5.00 p.m.
The 2026 Inlaks Theatre Awardees’ Showcase - 5.15 p.m. – 6.15 p.m.
Ek Mulaqat Manto Se - A Performance - 7.00 p.m. – 8.00 p.m.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
About the Inlaks Theatre Awardees’ Showcase
Held every year since 2023, the Inlaks Theatre Showcase offers a platform for the recipients of the theatre opportunities of that particular year to present their work and connect with the Inlaks theatre alumni community. This year’s showcase, featuring the presentations of the three 2026 theatre awardees, has been directed by 2016 Inlaks theatre awardee Kiyomi Mehta.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ek Mulaqat Manto Se
Language: Hindi, Urdu
Directed and performed by: Ashwath Bhatt
About the Performance
Saadat Hasan Manto is an Indo-Pakistani writer known for his irreverent and controversial writing. Hailed as one of Urdu's finest writers, he held up a mirror to society, especially in ugly times. The performance is based on Manto’s articles and explores his life and times, and the social changes he witnessed at the time of India’s Partition. Ashwath Bhatt plays Manto, who engages with the audience in trying to answer the larger question, “Why I write what I write”. The Manto that Ashwath plays, decodes the enigma and idiosyncrasies of Manto. Correlating his writing with the political climate of the time, this performance follows the writer as he contemplates his journey, changing mindsets, family life and poetry.

name: The World in the Body: Observe. Absorb. Create. - A Workshop by Tushar Pandey
description:
The World in the Body: Observe. Absorb. Create.
A Workshop by Tushar Pandey
This workshop explores the immense possibilities of the performer’s body and mind, and the relationship between the body, space and the world around us. Through observation, physical exploration and play, participants will draw from the rhythms, movements, textures and dynamics of nature, objects, people and spaces, allowing these external influences to become internal impulses and material for performance.
The work moves between the external and the internal: what moves us, what creates an impulse, and how physical sensation can lead to emotion, sound, words and eventually images.
Imagination and physicality become tools for exploring different theatrical languages, from realistic text and dramatic composition to epic storytelling and grotesque or comic worlds.
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Bhima
description:
Bhima
Language: English
Devised and performed by: Vivek Vijayakumaran and Sachin Gurjale
Directed by: Anitha Santhanam
Drawing inspiration from Ashok Malhotra’s Child Man, MT Vasudevan Nair’s Randamoozham, and Jeanette Winterson’s Weight, this play explores the paradoxes and ironies in the life of the second Pandava, Bhima.
Who is Bhima? What is his hunger? Who feeds it? What are the choices available to a hero? What is the fate of a strong man in contemporary times? These are some of the questions around which the key narrative of the play evolves. What is his relevance to contemporary life? Would his version of masculinity be acceptable in today’s world?
If Bhima were to live today, who would he be — a loyal middle-management warrior who is the engine of the company but never its CEO? A family man who defines himself only in terms of roles — the breadwinner, the husband, the son — who will do anything for his family? Or does he exist as an individual beyond these roles? Does society look after its Bhimas, or is it only Arjuna we want?
Contrasting the Koodiyattam form with contemporary dialogue and commentary, using music and poetry as interventions, Bhima re-examines a version of masculinity and its interaction with modernity.
Bhima won the Best Innovative Sound Design award for Sachin Gurjale at the 2017 Mahindra Excellence in Theatre Awards (META).
For enquiries please contact 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Physical Theatre: Its Possibilities and Limits - A Conversation with Tushar Pandey, Ashwath Bhatt and Vivek Vijayakumaran
description:
Physical Theatre: Its Possibilities and Limits
A Conversation with Tushar Pandey, Ashwath Bhatt and Vivek Vijayakumaran
Moderated by Anmol Vellani
Physical theatre communicates primarily, though not solely, through the language of gestures, facial expressions and movement. The exception is mime, which is non-verbal by definition.
In this session, three theatre artists will speak about what attracted them to physical theatre and describe the nature of their involvement in the teaching and practice of this stylised form of performance. As their work as directors and actors has also extended beyond physical theatre, they will reflect on the reasons for their divergent artistic choices.
Physical theatre has many strengths. Most notably, it can overcome language barriers, express what words cannot, connect with audiences at a visceral level, harness the ideas and creativity of the whole group, and rely on minimalist scenography. But equally, it is constrained by the very characteristics that set it apart from other theatre styles. This session will conclude with a discussion on the limits of physical theatre and the creative strategies that can prevent style from overshadowing substance.
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Red Nose Clowning - A Workshop by Ashwath Bhatt - Nov 23
description:
Red Nose Clowning
A Workshop by Ashwath Bhatt
The clown often lands in a place where urgency prevails and dilemma takes over, pressure turns into perseverance and a never-say-die attitude emerges. The clown lives in the moment, in a theatre of the 'Here and Now'.
Through the clown, participants will explore the world from a more positive viewpoint, free from moral and logical constraints. We all have a clown hiding within us. During the workshop, an inner clown character will be born through an organic process based on both eastern and western techniques. Starting with an outer neutral persona, we will work our way towards the ridiculous and then the grotesque.
At the end of the workshop, participants will gain clarity about the rules and tools of clowning, so that they can embark on clown exploration with courage. The workshop will go beyond gags and look for the clown who connects to the heart of the spectators.
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Uncle Dance
description:
Uncle Dance
Language: Hindi, English
Conceived and performed by: Pranjal Vaid with Jai Prakash Kumar
Age Limit: Above 18 years
Uncle Dance borrows from Pranjal’s personal struggles with patriarchy and with dance. It enquires into the quintessential uncle and the role of power and security in relationships and on the dance floor. The play also explores marriage as a construct, and the possibility of two people tying the knot to become one, when they are always actually two.

name: Lecture-Demonstration on the Folk Theatre of Bayalata - An Experience Sharing Session by Dr. Sahana Pinjar
description:
Lecture-Demonstration on the Folk Theatre of Bayalata
An Experience Sharing Session by Dr. Sahana Pinjar
Dr. Sahana Pinjar will be presenting a live demonstration of the traditional Kannada folk-theatre form of Bayalata through the performance of Girija Kalyana, depicting the divine marriage of Girija (Parvati) and Lord Shiva.  The demonstration will showcase the storytelling, acting, dialogue, traditional movements, music, costumes, and theatrical conventions of Bayalata, bringing the story to life for a contemporary audience. The story, written by Dr. Basavaraja Malshati, portrays Girija’s deep devotion and determination to attain Lord Shiva, her penance, and the eventual divine wedding. Through lively characters, expressive acting, traditional music and the energetic style of Bayalata, the narrative unfolds as both a sacred tale and a vibrant theatrical experience.
The performance celebrates themes of devotion, love, perseverance and the union of divine energies, while preserving the distinctive visual and performative elements of Karnataka’s folk theatre tradition.
For queries contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: MIRAGE: A Dramatic Reading
description:
MIRAGE: A Dramatic Reading
Language: English
Written by: Laya N Kumar
The war between the Pandavas and the Kauravas has long passed. Sanjeya, the royal chronicler and advisor to King Dhritarashtra, is on his deathbed. His gift of divine sight is long gone. But what he bore witness to during the war remains with him. He begins to narrate the tale of the war again — only this time, the tale is replete with events and details that he chose not to reveal during the war.
The play explores the following questions: What do we see but do not say? What stops us from speaking? What do we carry to our deathbeds? What does it mean to be a witness?
Mirage will be presented as a dramatic reading and incorporate elements of clowning.
The play reading will be followed by a discussion between the playwright, actors and  the audience.
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: The Death of Galileo
description:
The Death of Galileo
Language: Hindi
Directed by Rajkumar Rajak
About the Performance:
This play is an adaptation of Bertolt Brecht’s Life of Galileo. Using a non-linear theatrical structure, it connects Galileo’s struggle to contemporary realities.
The play unfolds at night inside a museum, where a group arrives to demolish its collection of cultural and collective living memories and objects. Among the artefacts, they discover a telescope, which becomes the point of departure for the story of Galileo — his discoveries, struggles, confinement and unceasing search for truth. As the night progresses, Galileo’s time and the present time begin to unfold simultaneously, revealing parallels between social realities in two different historical moments.
The members of the demolition group are themselves caught between disillusionment, violence and self-deception. Their encounter with the museum and with Galileo stirs their conscience, and while one group remains adamant, the other begins to question its reasons for wanting to destroy the museum. An internal conflict begins, between the path they’ve chosen, to raze the museum for their pride, and the path their conscience wants to guide them towards. Experimental music anchors the play in the present moment, voicing the characters' contradictions and a call to act for co-existence.
The performance draws on Brecht’s distancing effect alongside character expression, an actor-development process emerging from Rajkumar Rajak’s research.
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Stage Management - A Workshop by Abhishek Mudgal - Nov 26
description:
Stage Management
A Workshop by Abhishek Mudgal
Thursday to Saturday, 26th to 28th November, 10.00 a.m. - 3.00 p.m.
This introductory workshop is designed to give participants a practical understanding of the role of a stage manager and the stage management process in theatre.
The workshop will introduce participants to terminology and the various departments of theatre, followed by an exploration of the role and responsibilities of a stage manager across the different stages of a production — from pre-production and rehearsals to technical rehearsals and performances.
Participants will be introduced to basic stage management paperwork, organisational tools, communication practices and production processes. A key component will be crisis management, where participants will work through real-life theatre situations and learn to approach unexpected challenges with calm, logical and collaborative thinking.
The workshop will combine discussions, group activities, practical exercises and demonstrations, providing participants with a strong foundation in stage management.
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Writing Science Fiction Plays for the Indian Stage - A Conversation with Meghna Roy Choudhury and Abhishek Majumdar
description:
Writing Science Fiction Plays for the Indian Stage
A Conversation with Meghna Roy Choudhury and Abhishek Majumdar
Moderated by Anmol Vellani
After reading excerpts from their science fiction plays, two playwrights will converse on the nature of science fiction; why they chose to write speculative plays for the Indian stage; and whether they have been inspired or influenced by earlier Indian plays and performances in this genre. We will learn from them if writing science fiction for the theatre poses unique challenges. They will reference their own plays to demonstrate that science fiction is not a form of free-floating fantasy; it can, for instance, address moral dilemmas and ask searching questions about the political tendencies of our times.
Script Reading:
Juno 77
By Abhishek Majumdar
In Juno 77, a woman disappears during a space mission. Her partner’s search takes him far beyond Earth, where time unsettles everything they believed they knew about love, duty, and family. When their paths cross again, each has lived differently and in different references of time since the separation. How should they now understand their obligations to one another?
Against this story, Juno 77 asks questions at the heart of moral philosophy. Does an intention matter more than its consequences? Can someone be held to a promise in circumstances no one could have imagined? What does it mean to forgive a person whose absence has shaped your entire life?
The play also considers how religion helps us live with such questions. Faith offers ways to think about time, sacrifice, suffering and the possibility of reunion. Yet those ideas can mean different things to people who have endured the same loss differently. Bringing space science into conversation with religious thought, Juno 77 asks how we make moral choices when our shared understanding of a life has come apart.  It seeks to examine the question of whether our loves and losses are meaningful or mere coincidence.
Written and directed by Abhishek Majumdar, the play will be produced by Nalanda Arts Studio in Kannada and Hindustani versions.
The Archive on the Wall
By Meghna Roy Choudhury
The Archive on the Wall is a science fiction play inspired by holographic principle theory that explores memory, scientific thought, and political erasure, set inside a crumbling flat in contemporary Mumbai.
After her mother’s death, Aparna, a physicist turned archivist, returns to her childhood home to sort through her belongings. While scanning the old walls for data, she discovers that one wall retains more than structural history. It reacts. It hums. It remembers.
As the house approaches demolition, Aparna uncovers fragments of her mother’s political past, her own repressed memories, and traces of violence that were meant to disappear. She must confront what the wall has preserved and what she has chosen to forget.
The play asks what remains when history is erased, and whether memory can become an act of resistance.

name: Goonj ka Ghar
description:
Goonj ka Ghar
Language: Hindi (with subtitles in English)
Production co-ordinated by: Sanyukta Saha
About the Performance:
Goonj ka Ghar is a physical theatre performance that combines movement, minimal set design, and fragmented storytelling to explore themes of identity, power, and marginalisation. Initially inspired by three seminal short stories, Tirichh by Uday Prakash, Toba Tek Singh by Saadat Hasan Manto, and Uljhan by Vijaydan Detha, which are woven into a single theatrical narrative that interrogates unresolved questions of identity, belonging and justice in today’s world.
Set against the backdrop of a society grappling with citizenship, identity and social justice, the performance raises urgent questions: What makes a person a citizen? What do we call home when borders both physical and psychological remain in flux? Who is considered sane, worthy, beautiful, or legitimate? Why does society continue to value women who appear silent and submissive? Each segment reflects marginalisation through a distinct lens — surreal satire on madness and displacement, dark allegory on invisibility and class, and an introspective exploration of gender, self-worth and systemic injustice.
For enquiries please contact 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: How Not to Build a Theatre Institution - A Conversation with Abhishek Mudgal, Sanyukta Saha and Abhishek Majumdar
description:
How Not to Build a Theatre Institution
A Conversation with Abhishek Mudgal, Sanyukta Saha and Abhishek Majumdar
Moderated by Priyanka Varma
Artists establish and lead theatre institutions (which include long-standing initiatives) for different reasons — to practice, teach, present, advocate or support the art form, for instance.
But such undertakings, especially if they function independently of secure government or corporate largesse, can falter or fail. The poverty of infrastructure and support for the theatre are among the external factors that are adduced for the precariousness of artist-led institutions. Internal factors are rarely cited. What if the institution is over-reliant on personal equations and goodwill for its sustenance? Or if its ownership is narrowly concentrated in one or two charismatic personalities? Or if it is too obsessed with legacy concerns to avert obsolescence in a swiftly changing environment?
This session will investigate what might lie inside any theatre institution that could threaten its stability and hamper its growth. Reflecting on their personal experience of founding and running institutions, three theatre artists will tell us about what worked or did not work about the choices they made. Were discontents allowed to simmer, tensions swept under the carpet or challenges left unaddressed? In hindsight, do they regret any missteps or wish they had done some things differently?
For enquiries please contact: 50yearsofinlaks@gmail.com

name: Kadambari: Tracing Fragments of a Shattered Muse
description:
Kadambari: Tracing Fragments of a Shattered Muse
Language: Hindi, Bengali
Written and directed by: Meghna Roy Choudhury
Kadambari is a lyrical theatrical journey into the silenced life of Kadambari Devi, Rabindranath Tagore’s critic, muse, companion, and sister-in-law, married into the Tagore household at nine and gone by 25, when the poet himself was only 23. Rather than reducing her to a footnote in his biography, the play seeks to restore her voice, weaving memory, fiction and imagination. It traces fragments of her existence beyond whispers of scandal and tragedy, asking how history chooses to remember or erase the women who stand behind celebrated men.
Set during her final hours, the play imagines Death arriving to claim her. In this liminal space, Kadambari confronts Rabi with unresolved questions of love, freedom, and erasure. Their dialogue moves between the personal and the poetic, intertwining childhood memories, moments of intimacy, and echoes of Tagore’s fictional heroines who carry her shadow.
Kadambari won the award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role (Female) for Ipshita Chakraborty Singh at the 2026 Mahindra Excellence in Theatre Awards (META).

name: Dramatherapy - An Experience Sharing Session by Vardhan Deshpande
description:
Dramatherapy
An Experience Sharing Session by Vardhan Deshpande
In this session, Vardhan Deshpande reflects on his journey with Dramatherapy and its possibilities as a practice of healing, expression and transformation.
Over the past two-and-a-half years, he has been working with children at risk through Dramatherapy sessions, alongside six months of work with specially-abled children. This journey has involved much more than conducting sessions — it has been a continuous process of observing, designing, planning, facilitating, implementing, documenting and reflecting. Each group and every individual encounter has shaped his understanding of how theatre, play, imagination, embodiment, storytelling and creative expression can create spaces for children to explore themselves, connect with others and experience agency.
The session will share key experiences from this practice: the challenges encountered, the learning that emerged, the questions that continue to remain, and the ways in which reflection has influenced subsequent interventions. It will also look towards the future — considering how Dramatherapy and Applied Theatre can evolve in working with children and communities, and the ethical, creative and contextual sensitivities that such practice demands.

name: Tradition and Modernity in Contemporary Theatre
description:
Tradition and Modernity in Contemporary Theatre
A Conversation with Sharanya Ramprakash, Laya N Kumar and Parshathy J Nath
Moderated by Lakshmana KP
The traditions with which contemporary urban Indian theatre artists can engage are immense, embracing mythologies, folk tales and performances, art and craft objects and practices, festivals and rituals, cuisine, inherited knowledge and skills, and much else besides. At the same time, the distinction between the traditional and the modern is not clearcut. Modern theatre in India has a history that stretches back for over two centuries — long enough to develop its own traditions. Dance forms now regarded as ‘classical’ acquired modern practices of teaching, performance and patronage in the last century.
The theatre artists in this session will speak about their idea of tradition and how they have interacted with it in the plays they have written, directed or performed. They will also be invited to discuss ethical and political questions that come to the fore when tradition is brought into contemporary theatre work. Has their work been sensitive to the claim that borrowing from inherited forms of expression can constitute a form of cultural theft or disrespects localised and context-specific creation of value and meaning? How would they negotiate with traditions that have been invented in response to market demands or political pressures? Has their work reconciled with, or has it offered a critical perspective on the feudalism, casteism and gender discrimination embedded in many traditional performances and stories?

name: Full Frontal
description:
Full Frontal
Language: English
Co-created by: Abhay Mahajan and Sharanya Ramprakash
Performed by: Abhay Mahajan
About the Performance:
Enter Vinod. He is a man’s man. He is an actor. He is a lover. He is a delight. His gift is that he does not merely play a role — he becomes the role. Today, he is here to audition for perhaps his most difficult role yet: “A Feminist Man”.
Over the course of a 60-minute audition, guided by a disembodied voice — part director, part conscience, part societal echo — Vinod navigates the full range of his performative self. As memory, desire, myth, cinema and conditioning collide, the audition room becomes a space where masculinity is continuously performed, interrogated and disrupted.
Is a feminist man simply another role to master? Or is it something deeper, messier and impossible to fully perform? Blending humour, discomfort, role-play and self-examination, Full Frontal asks: what does it mean to be a man in India today?

name: Ritu Raga Rang: Seasons through Ragas - A multi-sensory experience through Hindustani music, art and aroma
description:
Ritu Raga Rang: Seasons through Ragas
The world of Hindustani classical music has been traditionally linked to the idea of seasons. Ancient Indian scriptures described six distinct seasons or ritus: Vasant (Spring), Grishma (summer), Varsha (monsoon), Sharad (Autumn), Hemant (Pre-Winter) and Shishir (Winter). Each of these seasons bring about different moods and feelings. In this multi-sensory performance, which includes Ragamala paintings and fragrances that evoke the feelings of each season, Nishant will paint portraits of the ritus using ragas and compositions as a canvas. This programme premiered at Stanford University to a warm reception and now comes to Bengaluru for the first time.
About the artist
Nishant Panicker is a Hindustani vocalist of the Agra-Atrauli gharana and a disciple of the late Vidushi Lalith J. Rao. He received his early training from the late sarod maestro Pandit Rajeev Taranath. At 15 he was a finalist in Naad Bhed, the national classical music talent search by SPIC MACAY and Doordarshan, and at 18 he was among the youngest recipients of the NCPA Hindustani Vocal Scholarship. He has performed at many prestigious venues across India and USA including the NCPA Mumbai, India International Centre Delhi, Bharat Bhavan Bhopal, Bangalore International Centre, Chowdiah Memorial Hall, Stanford University, Chinmaya Amarnath Pittsburgh and the Chhandayan Center in New York. He is also a regular performer in the music collective Sunaad.
Nishant is accompanied by Sri Udayaraj Karpur on tabla and Sri Surya Upadhyaya on harmonium.
